title: Native and Invasive Crayfish Species Impact on the Development of Fire Salamander Larvae: A Pilot Field Study From Northern Italy
content:
ABSTRACT

In northern Italy, the ongoing spread of non-native red-swamp crayfish Procambarus clarkii keeps indirectly decimating native populations of white-clawed crayfish Austropotamobius pallipes complex and is now also threatening local amphibians adapted to slow-flowing, hilly streams at the borders of its distribution. We conducted a preliminary field investigation into crayfish differential effects on the growth of fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) larvae. LMMs with orthogonal contrasts revealed that scaled mass index (SMI) was significantly higher for larvae living with native crayfish, while tail damage was mainly explained by SMI and missing limbs were too rare for statistical analysis. This may suggest stronger predation pressure or indirect effects on resource availability by P. clarkii, which could threaten previously unimpacted sites leading to unanticipated amphibians decline.
